questions.q: True or false? Your left back approaches the wide outlet, so the six should leave the middle to help.
questions.explain: Right, it's false. The six closes the central lane, so the deeper defenders keep a screen in front.
choiceExplanations: If the six leaves, the central lane opens and Blue's striker can receive in front of your defenders.
Right, it's false. The six closes the central lane, so the deeper defenders keep a screen in front.

questions.q: Blue breaks past your screen. Put these moments in order, first to last.
options: Left screen blocks the near outlet
Blue wins a loose inside pass
Blue passes around the screen wide
Midfielder recovers inside the delaying defender
questions.explain: Right. The screen sets up first, then Blue wins the ball, goes around it, and you recover.
choiceExplanations: Right. The screen sets up first, then Blue wins the ball, goes around it, and you recover.
Blue can only win that pass after the screen is already set during your attack.
Blue goes around the screen only after winning the ball in the middle.
Recovering comes last, once the pass has already gone beyond your screen.

questions.q: Now Blue goes around your right screen. Drag the six to rebuild protection in front of the defenders.
options: Join the defender at the ball
questions.explain: Yes. The six rebuilds the screen inside, so your defender can delay the winger with cover.
choiceExplanations: The passer no longer has the ball, so chasing leaves the lane inside your defender open.
Two players at the ball leave the inside lane free for a pass to Blue's striker.
Yes. The six rebuilds the screen inside, so your defender can delay the winger with cover.
